proposals.principle: An opening is passed only if overall width plus steering error fits; range is usable energy over energy per metre, and on this robot 2.66 of the 3.80 J/m on grass is electronics power over speed, so added cell mass barely raises J/m.
proposals.hypothesis: Inner width 11 cm gives 16 cm overall; with 1.0 cm steering sigma at full duty it fits the 20 cm opening offset +2 cm. Six AA cells (14.4 Wh, 12.2 Wh usable, 4 extra cells on hand, free) vs ~5.7 Wh needed at 0.49 kg (resistive term rises from ~1.14 to ~1.47 J/m). No catalogue swap is needed since both ranges contain the fix.
risks: shed: +108 g, but the traction limit of 26.1 deg on gravel does not depend on mass and the 16 N stall force is >3x the weight; 22 deg ramp still holds
kitchen/living_room/under_sofa: edge climbing is friction-limited (independent of mass); height unchanged at 6 cm < 9 cm overhang
proposals.result: not kept (another proposal gained more): gained bedroom, lawn, lost none; costs $0.00, 102 machine min

proposals.edit: locomotion -> tracks (idler_height=6.5, track_length=24); chassis (length=24, ride_height=2, width=10); battery -> liion_pack (capacity=28.2)
proposals.mechanism: step_higher_than_climbable (porch, 5.45 cm edge against at most 2.27 cm climbable), gap_longer_than_support (garden, 9.1 cm trench against a 6.0 cm wheel span), sinks_in_sand (sandbox, 2.97 kPa on 15 cm2 sinks 3.93 cm against 1.09 cm climbable)
proposals.principle: A track climbs any edge that meets its sloped front run, up to about its front idler height. A rigid vehicle bridges a gap while its centre of mass stays over support, about 0.45 of the track's contact length. Sinkage grows with ground pressure, which is weight over contact area.
proposals.hypothesis: No wheels4 value can fix these. A wheel never climbs more than its radius, and at most 4.5 cm is less than the 5.45 cm edge. A 9 cm wheel diameter is still narrower than the 9.1 cm trench. A rocker-bogie big enough for the step (r=6) stands about 14 cm and breaks under_sofa (9 cm). Tracks fix all three mechanisms. (1) Porch: an idler at 6.5 cm is above the 5.45 cm edge. (2) Garden: 0.45 x 24 cm = 10.8 cm of support, more than the 9.1 cm trench. (3) Sandbox: two long patches give roughly 100-150 cm2 of contact at about 0.7 kg, so about 0.5-0.7 kPa and under 1 cm of sinkage, below the 2 cm belly. Last time this was refused because the tub was too short for the track. Now the track is 24 cm and the tub is 24 cm, which is inside the allowed tub length of track length ±4 cm. Height is the idler at 6.5 cm plus 1.5 cm of track, so 8.0 cm, under the 9.0 cm sofa. Inner width drops to 10 cm to keep margin in the 20 cm bedroom door. Two things threaten the lawn survey: tracks roll harder, and the 1.8 cm sprocket cuts top speed to about 0.56 m/s at 100:1, so electronics cost about 4.6 J/m. That is about 7-9 J/m, or 35-45 kJ for 5 km, against only 44 kJ usable from the NiMH pack. So the battery moves to Li-ion at 28.2 Wh (3 cells, 138 g, lighter than the 162 g of NiMH), which roughly doubles the energy. The 100:1 N20 motors are kept: two motors on 1.8 cm sprockets give about 13 N at the ground, against about 3 N needed on the 22° ramp. The 5000 m at about 0.5 m/s takes about 10,000 s, under the 14,400 s limit. Cost: track kit $14, 3 cells at $4.5 plus a BMS at $1.5, so $29.00 in all, 4 days lead time, about 57 g of track print plus a tub reprint.
risks: under_sofa: overall height is about 8.0 cm against the 9.0 cm overhang. It holds if the track adds no more than the stated 1.5 cm above the idler.

bedroom: the overall width depends on how wide the tracks are. A 10 cm inner tub plus about 3 cm per side is about 16 cm, with 1.0 cm sigma, in a 20 cm opening. That is the same as the current 16 cm, which passes.
lawn: tracks cost more energy per metre and are slower. The 28.2 Wh Li-ion pack covers about 2x the estimated need, and the time is about 10,000 s against 14,400 s.
shed/kitchen/living_room: two motors instead of four, but the small sprocket keeps about 13 N at the ground. The steps (≤1.5 cm) are well under the idler height.
proposals.result: KEPT: gained garden, porch, sandbox, lost none; costs $29.00, 176 machine min

proposals.edit: locomotion -> tracks (idler_height=6, track_length=26); chassis (length=26, ride_height=2, width=10); battery (capacity=19.2)
proposals.mechanism: step_higher_than_climbable, gap_longer_than_support, sinks_in_sand (same three as above)
proposals.principle: Track front-idler climbing, a support span of 0.45 x contact length, and ground pressure as weight over area. The energy per metre cannot grow beyond the pack.
proposals.hypothesis: This is a cheaper hedge on the same mechanism that needs no Li-ion purchase. The tracks are 26 cm on a 26 cm tub, giving 0.45 x 26 = 11.7 cm of support over the 9.1 cm trench, and a longer patch for sand. The idler is at 6.0 cm, still above the 5.45 cm edge, with overall height 7.5 cm, leaving more margin under the 9 cm sofa. The NiMH pack goes to its maximum of 19.2 Wh (8 cells), and the 2 extra cells come free from the 4 on hand. That gives about 16.3 Wh (59 kJ) usable, against an estimated 35-45 kJ for the lawn. Cost: $14 track kit, 4 days.
risks: lawn: the energy margin is thinner than with Li-ion (59 kJ against about 45 kJ in the worst case), and the extra 54 g of cells raises rolling losses.
porch: with the idler at 6.0 cm, only about 0.55 cm above the edge, climbing depends on the sloped front run reaching it.
bedroom: same width reasoning as the first proposal, with a 10 cm inner tub.
proposals.result: not kept (another proposal gained more): gained garden, sandbox, lost none; costs $19.00, 184 machine min

iterations.notes: I swapped to tracks again because no wheel can fix the three failures. A wheel never climbs more than its radius, and the largest (4.5 cm) is below the 5.45 cm porch step. Its 9 cm diameter is also narrower than the 9.1 cm trench. Last time tracks were refused because the tub was too short. Here the tub length matches the track length, inside the allowed ±4 cm. The risk that has to be managed is energy on the 5 km lawn, so each proposal also changes the battery in the same edit. The first proposal costs $29.00 and 4 days, the second costs $14 and 4 days, and both fit the $57.50 / 7 day budget.
